about: Plain-language explanations of music and production jargon, used by ns['access_text'] (plain-language mode) and fl_describe. Each term: plain = a short explanation that fits in brackets after the word; level = basic (explained only in 'plain' mode) or pro (deep jargon: explained in 'plain' and 'standard' mode). aliases: other spellings matched the same way. Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive, first use only. Users can add or change terms in <state folder>/access/glossary.json (same format; their entries win).

LUFS.plain: loudness units: how loud it feels on average; -14 is a common streaming level, closer to 0 is louder

LU.plain: loudness units; 1 LU is a small step, 6 LU a big one

dB.plain: decibels: steps of loudness; 1 dB is barely noticeable, 6 dB is clearly louder

dBFS.plain: decibels below the digital maximum (0 dBFS is the ceiling)

dBTP.plain: true peak in decibels: the highest point of the waveform; above -1 risks distortion after streaming

true peak.plain: the very highest point of the waveform, between samples too

clipping.plain: the sound hitting the digital ceiling and getting cut off, which makes crackly distortion

headroom.plain: space left below the loudness ceiling

EQ.plain: equalizer: turns some pitch ranges up or down, like bass and treble knobs

high-pass.plain: a filter that removes the lowest sounds

low-pass.plain: a filter that removes the highest sounds

shelf.plain: an EQ move that raises or lowers everything above (or below) a point

compressor.plain: an effect that evens out loud and quiet moments

limiter.plain: an effect that stops the sound from going over a set ceiling

sidechain.plain: one sound briefly ducking out of the way when another plays (often the bass ducking for the kick)

ducking.plain: one sound getting quieter for a moment so another can be heard

reverb.plain: echo of a room or hall that makes a sound feel further away and bigger

delay.plain: an echo effect that repeats the sound

saturation.plain: gentle distortion that adds warmth and grit

pan.plain: where a sound sits from left to right

stereo.plain: sound that differs between the left and right speaker, so it feels wide

mono.plain: the same sound in both speakers, so it feels centered and narrow

correlation.plain: how alike the left and right sides are: 1 = identical (centered), 0 = very wide, below 0 = parts cancel out on one speaker

phase.plain: timing alignment of sound waves; out-of-phase sounds can cancel each other and go thin

mid/side.plain: splitting sound into the center part and the wide part

mud.plain: too much low-middle sound (200-500 Hz), which makes a mix cloudy

harsh.plain: too much upper-middle sound (about 2-6 kHz), which can feel piercing or tiring

presence.plain: the upper-middle range (about 2-5 kHz) where voices and attacks are clearest

air.plain: the very top of the sound (above about 8 kHz): sparkle and breath

sub.plain: the deepest bass (below about 60 Hz), felt as vibration more than heard

low end.plain: the bass range: kick drum and bass

low-mid.plain: the range just above the bass (about 200-500 Hz)

transient.plain: the sharp start of a sound, like the hit of a drum

release.plain: how quickly a sound or effect lets go after it stops

crest factor.plain: how much the peaks stick out above the average: high = punchy, low = squashed flat

dynamic range.plain: the difference between the quiet and loud parts

masking.plain: one sound hiding another because they share the same pitch range

resonance.plain: one narrow pitch that rings out louder than its neighbours

tilt.plain: whether the sound leans bright (more highs) or dark (more lows)

mastering.plain: the final polish that sets the overall loudness and tone of the finished song

mixing.plain: balancing all the parts' levels, tone and placement

mixer insert.plain: one channel strip on FL's mixer where a sound's effects and volume live

bus.plain: a mixer track that several sounds are sent to together

gain staging.plain: keeping levels sensible at each step so nothing distorts

automation.plain: a setting that changes by itself over time, like a fader that moves

velocity.plain: how hard a note is played (1-127)

quantize.plain: snapping notes exactly onto the beat grid

swing.plain: a bouncy, long-short rhythm instead of perfectly even notes

groove.plain: the rhythmic feel that makes you want to move

bar.plain: one measure of music, usually 4 beats

time signature.plain: how many beats are in each bar (4/4 = four, 3/4 = three, like a waltz)

key.plain: the home note and scale the song is built on

major.plain: a scale that usually sounds bright or happy

minor.plain: a scale that usually sounds darker or sadder

progression.plain: the order the chords come in

roman numeral.plain: a chord named by its step in the key (I = home chord, V = the chord that pulls home)

tonic.plain: the home note or home chord of the key

cadence.plain: a chord move that ends a phrase, like a musical full stop

modulation.plain: a change of key in the middle of a song

voicing.plain: how a chord's notes are spread out (close together or far apart)

register.plain: how high or low a part plays

octave.plain: the same note higher or lower (double or half the pitch)

semitone.plain: the smallest step between two notes (one piano key)

arpeggio.plain: the notes of a chord played one after another

ostinato.plain: a short pattern repeated over and over

pad.plain: a soft sustained sound that holds chords in the background

bassline.plain: the low tune played by the bass

kick.plain: the bass drum: the deep thump

snare.plain: the sharp crack drum, often on beats 2 and 4

hi-hat.plain: the small ticking cymbal that keeps time

timbre.plain: the color or character of a sound (what makes a flute and a violin sound different)

Hz.plain: hertz: vibrations per second; low numbers are low pitches

kHz.plain: thousands of vibrations per second: high pitches (1 kHz is roughly a whistle)

frequency.plain: how high or low a pitch is, measured in Hz

sample rate.plain: how many times per second the audio is measured (44100 or 48000 is normal)

bit depth.plain: how finely each audio sample is stored (24-bit is the usual for finished songs)

render.plain: turning the project into an audio file

stem.plain: an audio file of one part or group on its own

pattern.plain: a block of notes in FL that you place in the playlist

playlist.plain: FL's timeline where patterns and audio are arranged into a song

channel rack.plain: FL's list of instruments and samples

piano roll.plain: FL's note editor: pitch up and down, time left to right

plugin.plain: an instrument or effect that runs inside FL

preset.plain: a saved sound setting for an instrument or effect

MIDI.plain: note data (which key, when, how hard) without the sound itself

latency.plain: the small delay between playing and hearing

buffer.plain: a chunk of audio the computer prepares in advance; smaller = less delay but more strain

ASIO.plain: a fast audio driver type on Windows that lowers delay

normalization.plain: streaming services turning loud songs down (and sometimes quiet ones up) to an even level

width.plain: how spread out from left to right the sound feels

loopback.plain: recording what comes out of the speakers inside the computer
